patch.value: Fold pm package explore, inventory and manage into one installed-package listing with --depth brief|standard|deep, and align the SDK list target and the MCP package tool with it

Follow-up to pm-gh1777, which made pm package list an alias of the static inventory, gave every listing one --fields contract and dropped contributions from default explore/manage rows. Three listings of the same installed set remain, with different costs and evidence: inventory (static, offline, last observed update), explore (runtime-probed activation) and manage (runtime probe plus a live registry check that records update observations). The report's third suggestion was one command with --depth brief|standard|deep, as pm context does: brief = inventory rows, standard = explore activation status, deep = manage freshness. Two inconsistencies to settle in the same change: the SDK runExtension positional target list still maps to explore (src/sdk/extension.ts IMPLICIT_EXTENSION_ACTIONS), while the CLI list subcommand is the inventory; and the MCP pm_package tool exposes catalog/explore/manage but no inventory action (PM_EXTENSION_PACKAGE_ACTION_SUBCOMMANDS). Keep explore and manage as compatibility spellings. Duplicate check: searched fold package explore inventory manage depth listing; no open owner.

One installed-package listing takes --depth brief|standard|deep, where brief reads only manifests and saved state, standard adds the runtime activation probe, and deep adds the live registry check; The SDK list target, the CLI list subcommand and the MCP package tool resolve to the same listing; explore and manage keep working as compatibility spellings with unchanged output
An agent asks for installed packages once, chooses how much evidence to pay for with --depth, and gets the same listing from the CLI, the SDK and MCP

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Scope note from the PR #1782 review (Codex round 3): the CLI list alias now serves the static inventory, but PmClient.run('package list') is refused, the MCP pm_run action enum has no package-inventory, and PmClient.packageList() still runs the runtime explore listing (so --fields update is refused there). This item owns aligning those: add a canonical static listing action with the same --fields contract to the SDK and MCP dispatch, and document packageList() as the explore listing until the --depth listing lands.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: More scope from the PR #1782 review (Codex round 7): the command_output_contracts entry for package list/inventory inherits the package root's 3,000-token TOON budget (budgets are keyed by root command), while the static inventory applies no read-output controls; the --depth listing should declare its own budget per depth (brief unbudgeted, standard/deep budgeted), and the SDK packageList/extensionList helpers plus the native package target list should either route to the static listing or be documented as explore compatibility routes.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: More listing-surface scope from the PR #1782 review (Codex round 10): accept the --fields projection in the published inspectStaticExtensionInventory (so SDK hosts need not re-implement it, with the CLI delegating to it), and complete --fields on the package listing leaves (list, inventory, explore, manage, catalog) in bash, zsh and fish from the leaf flag contracts; completion currently takes package flags from the root contract only, which already left catalog --fields uncompleted on main.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 15 on PR #1782 repeated this scope: PmClient.packageList() still dispatches to explore (activation, rejects --fields name,version,update) and MCP has no package-list/inventory action; both move to the static reader and the shared projection here.
